correctness.rationale: PASS: For every fixed 0<r<1 and real periodic C3 boundary angle perturbation, the Poisson-smoothed curve is C2-close to radius-r circle and remains a strictly convex embedded Jordan curve for small epsilon. The full arclength expansion from U=iP_r(e^{iθ}h), V=-P_r(e^{iθ}h²)/2 yields first variation zero and second variation pi*r*epsilon² sum_{k!=0}(1-d_k²)|h_k|², d0=1,d1=r, d_k=r^{k-2}[(k+1)r²-(k-1)]/2. The constant rotation mode cancels. Parseval and pairwise ±k coefficients reconstruct the multipliers. For k>=3 analytic sign-splitting on t=r² gives |d_k|<r; the gap is 1-max(r²,((3r²-1)/2)²)>0 and equality directions switch at r=1/3. Independently tested exact rational frequencies 3..100 at five radii including r=1/3; all passed. Finite mode checks cannot prove the all-frequency inequality, which follows from the separate monotonicity argument. The O(epsilon³) remainder is only for fixed r,h; not uniformly high-frequency or endpoint.
